title: Sabbath: time to do good
body:
"Oh no, is Sabbath again!" was one thought that crossed my mind when I was a teenager. I knew that on Sabbath we rest, and it‘s a different day from all the days of the week, I knew what I wasn't able to do on Sabbath, but I was missing something important: What can I do on Sabbath that makes it really different and meaningful?

When I thought about rest my mind was stuck in waiting almost doing nothing until the day ended, without noticing I was minimizing the meaning of the Sabbath, that reminded me the problem that the leaders in the times of Jesus also had.
Back in the times of Jesus, the leaders distorted what was the Sabbath for, and they created special laws that they considered important to keep the Sabbath, but the reality is that they put a heavy burden that even them couldn't bear. 

How kept Jesus the Sabbath? 
Luke 4:16 (NIV) says "He went to Nazareth, where he had been brought up, and on the Sabbath day he went into the synagogue, as was his custom. He stood up to read,", so when we dedicate time to have communion with God and to share with our fellowships we know we are following Jesus example. But that's not the only activities that Jesus had this special day, Luke 13:10-17, John 5:1-15, Mark 3:1-6 tells us occasions where Jesus looked for people, stopped to hear, talked with them and healed during Sabbath hours, and in consequence He brought them freedom, happiness, peace, a new life during this special day. Jesus said in Matthew 12:11-12 "(...)“If any of you has a sheep and it falls into a pit on the Sabbath, will you not take hold of it and lift it out? How much more valuable is a person than a sheep! Therefore it is lawful to do good on the Sabbath.” in a unique call to reason about what it is important to do, considering that Sabbath was made for men (Mark 2:27) he expects us to have rest, peace, freedom, to be recreated, a moment that brings us healing. But he also expect us to bring the same to others that need it as much as we do.

How can I do good on Sabbath? I believe that there are many ways to do it, but we can start dedicating time to listen to others, maybe in our family, friends group or community is someone who is needing to be heard and comforted. 
We can also do good when we share a meal and a moment that can be refreshing for someone that had a busy or difficult week, or for someone that can‘t do it for its own. 
We can collaborate with God being the person that brings healing, through actions or words.
“It is always the right time to do what is right.” Martin Luther King Jr.
prayer:
Dear Heavenly Father,
I want to experience what you have for me during the Sabbath. And I also want to help others to receive the special blessings you have for us. While you bless me, help me bless others through actions and word.
In Jesus name I pray, Amen.
activity: Visit someone who cannot attend church because of illness or age. If you want to take it one step more, consider doing it for people that might not be part of the church, can be a family member, a friend or neighbor.
